title: Role changes and suspensions in Members have no effect on what the person can do
detail: orgApi.changeRole and setSuspended only update d.members. The session role comes from the user directory (store/session.ts:63, useRole returns s.user.role from userById), so every UI gate (useCan, useCanDo) ignores the change. Most backends do too: agents/backend.ts requireRole (line 57), platform.runKeyCeremony and upgradePlan all read userById(...).role. api.signIn (api/index.ts:49) never checks member status. So an admin demoted to viewer can still add, retire and delete agents, rotate keys and grant autonomy, and a suspended member can sign in and act. The dialogs say the opposite: 'The change applies at their next request' (line 249) and 'sign-in is refused' (line 263).
fix: Add a helper effectiveRole(orgId, user) = db.getDB(orgId).members.find(m => m.userId === user.id)?.role ?? user.role, returning undefined when status === 'suspended'. Use it in useRole, useCan (session.ts:63-64) and useCanDo (permissions.ts:49); subscribe via db.subscribe so they re-render on 'member'. Replace the userById-based requireRole in agents/backend.ts:57, work/backend.ts:108 and platform.ts:1689, and the check in platform.runKeyCeremony:678, with the member-aware logic from orgApi.ts:89-93. The Members dialog copy at line 249 then becomes true.
repro: Sign in as an owner, open /agents/people and change an admin to Viewer. Sign in as that admin: /agents/new still shows the wizard and createAgent succeeds. Suspend a member, then sign in as them: it works.
verifyNote: The role half is confirmed. orgApi.changeRole (orgApi.ts:654) mutates only d.members. useRole and useCan (store/session.ts:63-64) and useCanDo (permissions.ts:49) read s.user.role, which comes from the USERS directory via userById. agents/backend.ts:57, work/backend.ts:108 and platform.ts:1689/678 all check userById().role, so a demoted admin keeps admin powers in both the UI and the backends. Only orgApi.requireRole (orgApi.ts:89-93) uses the member role. The suspension half is overstated: LoginPage.tsx:68 and :207 and registry.ts:390 and :510 already refuse sign-in for a suspended member. What remains is that the backends do not check member status for an already-loaded session.

title: next= validation lets '/\host' through, and MaintenancePage accepts '//host'; navigate then throws SecurityError
detail: destination() rejects only '//' prefixes. A `next` of `/\evil.example` passes, and so does `/%5Cevil.example` once decoded. The browser URL parser treats the backslash as a slash, so `history.replaceState` (navigate with replace:true) throws a cross-origin SecurityError. The session has already started, but the user stays on the sign-in page with an uncaught error. MaintenancePage.tsx:23 checks only `startsWith('/')`, so `?next=//evil.example` breaks 'Continue to the console' the same way.
fix: Add a shared helper `safeNext(next)` that returns `next` only when `/^\/(?![\/\\])/.test(next)`, `!/[\x00-\x1f\\]/.test(next)` and `new URL(next, location.origin).origin === location.origin`, and returns undefined otherwise. Use it in LoginPage.destination (which also covers AcsPage) and in MaintenancePage's `back`.
repro: Open /login?next=%2F%5Cevil.example and sign in with a demo account. Nothing happens, and the console shows a SecurityError.
verifyNote: Confirmed. This is the same root cause as #6. LoginPage.tsx:26 rejects only a leading '//', and MaintenancePage.tsx:23 checks only startsWith('/'). With BrowserRouter, history.replace calls replaceState with no try/catch, so '/\host' or '//host' throws a SecurityError. Through the push path the browser leaves the site instead (see #6), so the severity is critical, not medium.

title: Open redirect through ?next= after sign-in
detail: destination() accepts any `next` that starts with '/' and not '//'. A value such as `/\evil.com` (or `/%09/evil.com`) passes the check, but the browser URL parser treats `/\` as `//`, so it resolves to https://evil.com. The 'Continue' button for an already signed-in user (line 276) calls nav(destination(current, next)) with push; history.pushState throws SecurityError on the cross-origin URL and @remix-run/router's push() then falls back to window.location.assign(url), which sends the user to the attacker's site. The finish() and AcsPage paths use replace, which throws instead: the session has already started, so the user is signed in but sees a raw 'Failed to execute replaceState' error. MaintenancePage.tsx:23 has the same weak check (`startsWith('/')` only), so `/maintenance?next=//evil.com` makes 'Continue to the console' throw.
repro: While signed in, open /login?next=%2F%5Cexample.com and click Continue. The browser leaves for example.com.
fix: Add a shared `safeNext(next: string | null): string | undefined` helper. Reject anything that fails `/^\/(?![\/\\])/`, contains a backslash or control character, or whose `new URL(next, location.origin).origin` is not location.origin. Return `u.pathname + u.search + u.hash` when it passes. Use it in LoginPage.destination and in MaintenancePage (`const back = safeNext(sp.get('next')) ?? '/'`).
verifyNote: Confirmed against the installed @remix-run/router (router.js:363-384). In push(), a failed pushState that is not a DataCloneError falls back to `window.location.assign(url)`. destination() accepts '/\evil.example' (also '/%5Cevil.example', and '/\t/evil' after tab stripping). The signed-in user's 'Continue' button (LoginPage.tsx:276) calls nav() with push, so pushState throws a cross-origin SecurityError and the browser goes to evil.example. finish() and AcsPage use replace, which has no try/catch, so they throw after the session has started. MaintenancePage.tsx:23 accepts '//evil.com' and throws the same way.

title: Emergency-stop re-authentication password is never checked
detail: When the last sign-in is older than 10 minutes, the dialog asks for 'Your password' (lines 106-109). `ready` only requires password.length >= 4, and engage() calls markReauth() without checking the password at all. Any 4 characters pass the re-authentication gate. markReauth() then also resets signedInAt, which extends the session (see the separate finding). DecisionForm does check the password, through `reauth` from '@/features/work/backend'.
repro: Sign in, wait more than 10 minutes (or set signedInAt back in localStorage eg:session), open Emergency stop, type 'xxxx' as the password plus a reason and STOP. The stop engages.
fix: In StopDialog.engage: `if (reauth) { try { await reauth(user.id, password) } catch (e) { setPwError((e as Error).message); setBusy(false); return; } markReauth(); }`. The reauth function comes from '@/features/work/backend'; rename the local `reauth` boolean (e.g. needPw) so it does not shadow the import. Show pwError on the password Field.
verifyNote: Confirmed. StopDialog.tsx:35 only requires `password.length >= 4`, and engage() at line 41 calls markReauth() without checking the password. markReauth also resets signedInAt, so any 4 characters pass the 10-minute re-authentication gate and extend the session. DecisionForm checks the password before calling markReauth.

title: Set-up wizard is open to every role, including viewer and auditor
detail: /onboarding is wrapped only in RequireAuth (App.tsx:106), and OnboardingPage has no role check. Any signed-in viewer, approver or read-only auditor can open it and press 'Finish set-up'. completeOnboarding() then enables frameworks through api.setFramework (no role check), creates the starter rulebook draft and draft agent through db.starterFromOnboarding, and writes 'onboarding.completed' and 'rulebook.drafted' receipts in their name. It also overwrites the organisation's saved onboarding state, since saveOnboarding runs on every patch. Only the level, identity, packs, invites and updateOrg steps are role-gated.
repro: Sign in as a viewer or the auditor, go to /onboarding, click Continue through the steps and finish. Frameworks get enabled and a starter rulebook draft appears under the user's name.
fix: See #30.
verifyNote: Confirmed. This duplicates #30. The /onboarding route has only RequireAuth, and OnboardingPage has no role check. completeOnboarding runs api.setFramework (no role check, api/index.ts:365), db.starterFromOnboarding plus logAdmin 'rulebook.drafted', a direct mutation of d.org.legalEntity (line 66) and logAdmin 'onboarding.completed' for any role.

title: decide() records approval.partial during an emergency stop (open item c confirmed)
detail: In decide(), when needsTwo() is true and there is no first approval yet, the function writes an 'approval.partial' admin receipt and stores x.partials[a.id] (lines 189-195) BEFORE ever calling db.decideApproval(), which is the only place decisionBlocked() (stop check) runs. So while an emergency stop covers the agent, a first approval of a large payment is accepted and signed onto the chain, and after the stop is lifted only one more click is needed. The same bypass exists in decideByLink() (lines 222-234).
fix: In work/backend.ts decide(), right after the 'no longer waiting' check: `const blocked = api.decisionBlocked(orgId, a.id); if (blocked) throw new Error(blocked);`. Add the same check in decideByLink() after the approval lookup, using link.orgId, so the partial branch cannot run either.
repro: Sign in as an owner at org_northbank (two-person on at L2), engage the emergency stop, open a pending approval with amount >= â‚¹10,00,000, click First approval and commit: toast 'First approval recorded' and an approval.partial receipt appears although the stop holds the approval.
verifyNote: Confirmed. In work/backend.ts, decide() (lines 189-195) and decideByLink() (lines 222-234) write an approval.partial receipt and set x.partials before any stop check. decisionBlocked only runs inside db.decideApproval (db.ts:939), and engageStop sets heldByStop on pending approvals (db.ts:1031). So during a stop a first approval is signed onto the chain, and once the stop is lifted only one more click is needed.

title: Supplied key fingerprint passes if it matches any key in the bundle, even one that signed nothing
detail: The keys section accepts `--fingerprint` when `allFps.includes(supplied)`. The fingerprints come from every entry in `public_keys`, and nothing checks that the matching key actually signed any receipt or the manifest. A forger can keep the organisation's real public key in `public_keys` as an unused entry, add their own key, and sign every receipt (and the L2 manifest via `signing_kid`) with it. Section 2 then reports 'matches the bundle's key', the signatures verify and the result is PASS. This defeats the out-of-band anti-substitution check that PASS (as opposed to PASS_KEY_FROM_BUNDLE) is meant to represent.
repro: Export a pack, add a key `k_evil` to public_keys, and re-sign every receipt and the manifest with it (keep the real kid's public key in the map). Verify with the real fingerprint: the result is PASS.
fix: In verify6.ts section 2, compare `supplied` with the head key's fingerprint (`fingerprint`, line 245). At L2, also compare it with sha256Hex(keys[m.signing_kid]).slice(0,16). For receipts signed by older kids, accept a kid only when a key.rotated receipt in the bundle, signed by an already-trusted kid, names it as new_kid. Otherwise call fail() and report FAIL_INTEGRITY. Put allFps only in the facts or diagnostics, never in the pass condition.
verifyNote: Confirmed at verify6.ts:246-258. allFps is built from every entry in `keys`, and the check is `supplied && !allFps.includes(supplied)`. A supplied fingerprint that matches any key in the bundle gives 'pass', even when that key signed no receipt and not the manifest. The manifest signer (line 219, `m.signing_kid`) is taken from the bundle and never tied to the supplied fingerprint, so a substituted signing key with the real key left in as an unused decoy gives PASS rather than PASS_KEY_FROM_BUNDLE.

title: Role changes and member removal are never enforced: checks read the global User.role and orgIds, not the org member record
detail: orgApi.changeRole/removeMember only change `db.members`. `requireRole` (platform.ts:1689), `runKeyCeremony` (678), `approveReview` (1375), `upgradePlan` (600) and `reviewsQueue` (1392) all use `userById(id).role` and `u.orgIds`, which never change. Likewise `useRole`/`useCan` in store/session.ts:63-64 read `s.user.role`. So an admin demoted to viewer keeps every admin power (grants, erasures, packs, counterparties, key ceremonies, reviews), and a removed admin still passes. In decideApproval (db.ts:945), a removed owner has no member record, so the code falls back to `user.role === 'owner' && user.orgIds.includes(orgId)`, and a removed owner can still decide outside the group.
repro: As the owner, change u_rahul to viewer in People and roles. Sign in as Rahul: he can still run a key ceremony, set autonomy grants and approve rulebook reviews. Remove an owner: they can still approve any approval as an owner override.
fix: Add one helper in db.ts, `memberRole(orgId, userId): Role | undefined`, that returns the role of the member record with status 'active' (undefined when the record is missing, invited or suspended). Use it in platform.ts requireRole, runKeyCeremony, approveReview, upgradePlan and reviewsQueue, in agents/backend.ts and work/backend.ts requireRole, and in decideApproval and issueApprovalLink (drop the fallback to `user.role`). In session.ts, have useRole and useCan read memberRole(s.orgId, s.user.id) ?? (auditor role from s.user), and subscribe to db 'member' events so a role change re-renders.
verifyNote: Confirmed. orgApi.changeRole and removeMember (orgApi.ts:643-704) change only db.members. platform.ts requireRole (1689), runKeyCeremony (678), approveReview (1375), upgradePlan (600) and reviewsQueue (1392) read userById(id).role and orgIds. So do features/agents/backend.ts:57 and features/work/backend.ts:108. On the client, useRole and useCan (session.ts:63-64) and TopBar (`can(user?.role,'stop.engage')`) read the global User.role. decideApproval (db.ts:945) falls back to the global owner role when the member record is gone. A demoted or removed admin or owner therefore keeps their powers. orgApi's own requireRole (orgApi.ts:89) already reads the member record, which shows the intent.

title: upgradeLevel is not atomic; an upgrade to L3 or Sovereign throws halfway for a sign-up organisation
detail: upgradeLevel first appends `level.upgraded`, which emits and saves, then sets `levelHistory` and `plan`, and only after that calls runKeyCeremony. runKeyCeremony needs 3 key holders from L3 upwards, but custodyHolders() for a fresh organisation lists only its active owners and admins, usually just the creator. It throws 'needs 3 of 1 key holders'. At that point the organisation is already on L3 (persisted): there is no HSM key, no carried-over A3 grants (so every write is refused as 'A0 Observe (no grant)'), billing is not re-derived and syncOrgMeta is not called. upgradePlan reports allowed: true, so nothing warns first.
repro: Sign up a new organisation (only the creator is a member). In Assurance levels, upgrade L1 â†’ L3: an error appears, yet the organisation now shows L3 and every agent write is refused.
fix: In platform.ts upgradePlan: when levelRank(to) >= 2, `db.fresh` and custodyHolders(db).length < 3, set whyNot ('A key ceremony needs 3 key holders; add at least 3 owners or admins first'). In upgradeLevel: do all checks, including the holder count, before append. Snapshot db.org.plan and levelHistory and wrap the rest in try/catch that restores them on a throw, or reorder so the ceremony runs and validates before level.upgraded is appended.
verifyNote: Confirmed at platform.ts:610-645. upgradeLevel appends level.upgraded, then sets levelHistory and plan, and only then calls runKeyCeremony (629). For a sign-up organisation, custodyHolders (188-192) lists only its active owners and admins, usually just the creator. With participants undefined, present = holders.slice(0,3) has length 1, which is below quorumNeeded 3, so it throws after the organisation is already at L3 (saved by append â†’ emit). The grants carry-over, deriveBilling and syncOrgMeta never run. This is reachable from onboarding (complete.ts:77) and from UpgradePage. upgradePlan reports allowed: true.

title: Two separate autonomy-raise systems with different two-person rules
detail: AutonomyPage uses autonomyApi.requestGrant, stored in d.autonomyLocal.requests, and asks for a second person only when raising to A4 or A5 (twoPerson = enforced && raise && rank>=4). Any raise to A1â€“A3 goes straight through api.setGrant from a single person. The agent's Autonomy tab (AgentAutonomy â†’ backend.changeGrant, line 509) treats every raise as a two-person change and stores requests in d.agentsExt.grantRequests. Neither screen shows the other's pending requests, and their duplicate guards are separate. The result: (a) a single admin can take a tool from no grant to A3 on /agents/autonomy, although the agent tab, the Roles banner and EG-16 say raises need two people; (b) a raise requested on one screen never appears for approval on the other.
fix: In AutonomyPage GrantDialog.submit, replace the twoPerson/api.setGrant branches with `const r = await changeGrant(orgId, input, user.id)` from '@/features/agents/backend', and toast according to r.kind. Change the twoPerson condition to `enforced && (raise || widerBound)`. Make ProposalsPanel/pending lists read grantRequests(orgId) and act through decideGrantRequest. Delete autonomyApi.requestGrant and decideRequest, or have them delegate to the backend functions.
repro: On org_kaveri (L3), as an owner, open /agents/autonomy and choose 'Change level' on a write tool with no grant. Pick A3 and press Grant: the grant is written at once. Do the same on /agents/<slug>?tab=autonomy: it records a request for a second person.
verifyNote: Confirmed. AutonomyPage GrantDialog (lines 446-469) requires a second person only when raising to rank >= 4. Raises to A1-A3 call api.setGrant directly. Requests are stored by autonomyApi.requestGrant (autonomyApi.ts:97-108) in a separate store. agents/backend.changeGrant (backend.ts:498-520) treats every raise, including a wider A4 bound, as two-person and stores requests in agentsExt.grantRequests. The two stores and their duplicate guards are disjoint.

title: L2 KMS key rotation on Agents â€º Keys â€º Custody skips the required second person
detail: On Proof â€º Keys (KeysCustody.tsx) an L2 rotation is dual control: one person requests (key.rotation.requested) and a different owner or admin approves. CustodyTab on /agents/keys?tab=custody shows a 'Rotate the KMS key' button to any owner or admin. Its CeremonyWizard (l3 false, step 2) calls api.runKeyCeremony directly (line 222), so one person rotates the KMS key alone. Better, reuse the KeysCustody component, or link to /evidence?tab=keys. In platform.runKeyCeremony, when level === 'l2' and kind === 'rotation', require an open key.rotation.requested receipt whose actor !== userId (callers from upgrade at lines 629/640 pass kind 'generation' and stay exempt).

title: Focus trap re-runs whenever onClose changes identity, so focus jumps while the user types
detail: useFocusTrap's effect depends on [open, onClose]. Almost every caller passes an inline arrow function as onClose, so any re-render of the parent re-runs the effect. The cleanup focuses `prev`, and the new run focuses [data-autofocus] or the first focusable element (the header Close button) 20 ms later. Examples in scope: (1) YouPage TwoStep dialog: TwoStep re-renders every second (tick interval) and on every keystroke (setCode), so focus moves from the code input to the Close button and the 6-digit code cannot be typed. (2) Onboarding PeopleStep Slack dialog: each keystroke in Workspace calls setWorkspace, which re-renders the parent, so focus jumps to Close after every character. (3) StopDialog and ShortcutsDialog in AppShell: AppShell re-renders on every live-traffic receipt (about every 5-14 s through useOrgVersion), so focus is pulled from the Reason or password field back to the STOP input. (4) LoginPage SsoDialog: PasswordSignIn re-renders every second (setNow interval), so keyboard focus is pulled back to the email field and the provider buttons cannot be reached with Tab. The effect also toggles body overflow on every run.
repro: Go to /you, click 'Set up two-step sign-in' and type a digit in 'Code from your app'. Focus moves to the dialog's Close button.
fix: In overlay.tsx useFocusTrap: `const cb = useRef(onClose); cb.current = onClose;`, call `cb.current()` in onKey, and change the effect dependencies to `[open]`. This fixes every Dialog and Drawer at once.
verifyNote: Confirmed. useFocusTrap's effect depends on [open, onClose]. When it re-runs, the cleanup focuses `prev` and the new run focuses [data-autofocus] or the first focusable element 20 ms later. AppShell passes `onClose={() => setStopOpen(false)}` inline and re-renders on every live receipt through useOrgVersion, so focus is pulled from the Reason or password field back to the STOP input. LoginPage's SsoDialog gets an inline onClose, and PasswordSignIn re-renders every second (setNow), so focus snaps back to the email input every second and keyboard users cannot stay on the provider buttons. Body overflow is also toggled on every re-run.

title: A second emergency stop can be engaged while one is active, which orphans the first incident and unfreezes its approvals
detail: IncidentsPage disables the stop while one is active ('Only one stop is open at a time'). The TopBar button and the command palette's 'Emergency stopâ€¦' (CommandPalette.tsx:100) are always enabled for owners and admins. After a selective stop, a second selective stop on other still-active agents calls db.engageStop, which overwrites db.stop with the new incidentId, scope and agentSlugs. The first incident stays 'active' forever, because liftStop only resolves db.stop.incidentId. stopCovers() now only covers the second stop's agents, so approvals held by the first stop become decidable while their agents are still stopped.
repro: As an owner, run Emergency stop â†’ Selected agents â†’ pick agent A. Open it again from the top bar â†’ Selected â†’ pick agent B. A's waiting approvals can now be approved, and A's incident never resolves.
fix: In TopBar, disable the Emergency stop button when db.getDB(orgId).stop.active, with the same 'Only one stop is open at a time' tooltip as IncidentsPage. In CommandPalette, hide the item when stop.active. In db.engageStop, throw 'A stop is already engaged. Lift it before engaging another.' when db.stop.active. Optionally make stopCovers honour `a.heldByStop` so frozen approvals stay blocked.
verifyNote: Confirmed. TopBar.tsx:79 and the palette item at CommandPalette.tsx:100 are always enabled for owners and admins. db.engageStop (db.ts:1012-1035) overwrites db.stop without checking stop.active. stopCovers (db.ts:917) only looks at the current db.stop.agentSlugs, so approvals frozen by the first selective stop become decidable. liftStop resolves only db.stop.incidentId, so the first incident stays 'active' forever. IncidentsPage and AlertsPage already disable the stop while one is active.

title: decideByLink partial path skips approver-group membership; console partial path uses stale global role
detail: decideByLink() only checks link.issuedTo === userId; in the two-person branch it writes approval.partial without calling mayDecide()/allowedApprovers(), so a person removed from the approver group (or suspended) after the link was issued can still give the first approval. In decide(), mayDecide() (line 135-144) grants the owner override from userById(userId).role (static demo user), not the org member record, so a suspended or demoted owner passes the partial step while db.decideApproval (which uses db.members status/role) would refuse the final one.
fix: In work/backend.ts mayDecide(), compute owner as `const rec = db.getDB(orgId).members.find(m => m.userId === userId); const owner = rec ? rec.status === 'active' && rec.role === 'owner' : !!u && u.role === 'owner' && u.orgIds.includes(orgId);` (the same rule as db.decideApproval). In decideByLink, before the needsTwo branch, add `const who = mayDecide(link.orgId, a, userId); if (!who.ok) throw new Error(who.why);`. secondApprovals() inherits the corrected mayDecide.
repro: Issue a single-use link to a finance member, then remove that member from the Finance group in People and roles; open the link signed in as them and give the first approval on a two-person amount â€” it is recorded.
verifyNote: Confirmed. decideByLink's partial branch (lines 222-234) only checks link.issuedTo === userId and never checks group membership. The full path does check it, via api.decideByLink â†’ db.decideApproval â†’ allowedApprovers. Separately, mayDecide (lines 139-142) grants the owner override from the static userById().role, while db.decideApproval (db.ts:944-945) uses the db.members record (status 'active' and role 'owner'). A suspended or demoted owner, or a person removed from the group, can therefore give the first approval of a two-person decision.

title: Approval.heldByStop is not shown or honoured anywhere in the approvals UI (open item a confirmed)
detail: No file under src/features references heldByStop or api.decisionBlocked. ApprovalDetail computes `decidable = pending && !expiredNow && canDecideRole && who.ok` with no stop check, so Approve/Reject stay enabled, the form asks for a reason and password, and only the backend throws (or, with two-person, silently records a partial â€” see backend finding). The inbox Row (ApprovalsPage.tsx 235-268), the Today WaitingPanel, secondApprovals().canAct and LinksSection (which lets you 'Send a single-use link' that then fails in issueApprovalLink) also show held approvals as actionable.
fix: In ApprovalDetail DetailBody add `const held = api.decisionBlocked(orgId, a.id);`. Change to `decidable = pending && !held && !expiredNow && canDecideRole && who.ok` and put `held` first in noDecideWhy. Render a held-tone Banner with the reason and a link to /incidents/<a.heldByStop.incidentId>, and render LinksSection only when `pending && !held`. In ApprovalsPage Row show a 'Held by the stop' badge when a.heldByStop is set. In work/backend.ts secondApprovals(), set canAct=false and whyNot to the decisionBlocked text when it returns one.

title: Reviews signs off assessments through the legacy api.reviewAssessment, bypassing pack-admission gates and status checks
detail: ReviewCard calls api.reviewAssessment (api/index.ts 342) instead of the assessments backend reviewAssessment. title: Re-route lets an admin move any approval to their own group and then approve it; no role, status or stop checks
detail: `reroute()` has no permission check and no `a.status === 'pending'` check. verifyNote: Confirmed at db.ts:983-995. reroute() has no status, permission or stop check, and the target is pushed into `escalations`. allowedApprovers (line 912) then counts members of every from/to group as approvers. The UI does show Reroute only for pending approvals and only with approvals.reroute (owner or admin), so this is high, not critical: it needs an admin, but it defeats the owners-only rule.

title: A selective emergency stop refuses every agent, not only the selected ones
detail: governCall refuses with 'Emergency stop engaged' whenever `db.stop.active`, whatever the scope. engageStop with `slugs` marks only the selected agents as 'stopped' and records scope 'selected_agents', but every other active agent's live calls are then refused with rule agent-paused, inflating the refusals billed at 0.4. stopCovers() (line 917) already implements the correct scope test for approvals.

title: The live guard never applies the published rulebook (or switched-off tools); the decision comes from the scenario
detail: governCall stamps the receipt with the current published rulebook version and hash, but takes `decision/ruleId/reason` from the hard-coded scenario `call`. A rulebook published from the console, for example one that refuses gmail.send_email, has no effect on live decisions. Receipts then claim a rulebook version whose rules contradict the decision. Tools switched off via api.setToolEnabled are also still allowed, despite EG-01 ('unknown and switched-off tools are refused').

fix: In governCall, after the stop and pause check: if the tool is disabled on its connector (db.connectors.flatMap(c=>c.tools).find(t=>t.name===call.tool)?.enabled === false), refuse with rule_id 'tool-disabled'. Otherwise run `const e = evaluate(rb?.rules ?? [], call.tool, call.args, call.tags)` and use e.decision, e.ruleId and e.reason as the input to applyAutonomy and the receipt. Take approverGroup and expiresInH from the matched rule (rule.approver, rule.expiresIn) when present, and use the scenario only for the headline and effect text.
verifyNote: Confirmed at db.ts:776-797. The receipt is stamped with the published rulebook's version and hash, but decision, ruleId and reason come from the scenario `call`. evaluate() is never called, and connector tool `enabled` flags are never checked. A newly published rulebook or a switched-off tool has no effect on live decisions, and receipts cite a rulebook whose rules contradict their decision.

detail: dataPolicy() reports retention as max(set retention, compliance lock years), so the Close dialog (Organisation.tsx line 243) promises 'Receipts are kept until <now + 10 years>' on org_deccan (Ceph lock 10 years, default retention 8). scheduleClosure computes retentionUntil from the raw s.retention.years (8). title: Each fresh sign-in (re-auth) adds a duplicate session for the same browser
detail: The current session id is `ses_${user.id}_${signedInAt}`, and the effect on line 25 registers a session whenever signedInAt changes. markReauth() (used by the autonomy grant, the upgrade confirm and approvals) rewrites signedInAt, so a new session record is created. The earlier record for the same browser stays open and is listed under 'other sessions', with Sign out and 'Sign out other sessions' offered for it.

verifyNote: Confirmed. currentId is `ses_${user.id}_${signedInAt}` (Sessions.tsx:23), and registerSession (orgApi.ts:257-266) creates a new record whenever the id is new. markReauth (session.ts:85-90) rewrites signedInAt, so the effect (Sessions.tsx:25-27, and YouPage.tsx:44) registers a second record. title: The auditor's cross-organisation check verifies against the key the receipt carries
detail: checkCrossOrg verifies the signature with x.publicKey (the key embedded in the received receipt). When the client has pinned no fingerprint, the Issuer key step is 'skip' and a self-signed forgery returns 'verified', which is written to the working papers as 'Verified by you'. title: Receipt search by '#4097' or '4,097' always shows 'No match'
detail: useMemo strips '#' and ',' from the query to find receipts. The Command.Item value is `receipt ${seq} ${hash}`, and cmdk keeps filtering with its default fuzzy scorer against the raw input. Every query character must appear in the value, so '#' and ',' score 0 and the receipt item is hidden. Checked against the installed cmdk 1.1.1: defaultFilter('receipt 4097 9c1eâ€¦', '#4097') returns 0, and the same call with '4097' returns 0.891. The placeholder specifically suggests 'a receipt number like #4097', and seqLabel shows numbers as '#4,097'.

fix: In CommandPalette.tsx:50 pass `keywords={[`#${r.seq}`, seqLabel(r.seq), String(r.seq)]}` to Command.Item (extend the Item helper to accept keywords), or include them in the value: value={`receipt #${r.seq} ${seqLabel(r.seq)} ${r.seq} ${r.hash}`}.
verifyNote: Confirmed. Running cmdk's commandScore from node_modules gives commandScore('receipt 4097 9c1eab', '#4097') = 0, '4,097' = 0 and '4097' = 0.891. useMemo strips '#' and ',' to find receipts, but cmdk's built-in filter scores the raw input against the Item value, so the receipt row is hidden and 'No match' appears. detail: DETECTORS (alerts/detectors.tsx 48-65) and the Alerts page copy ('6 detectors compare each agent with its own baseline') present new_counterparty and off_hours as live detectors with on/off switches and sensitivity, but detectFor() only implements refusal_surge, amount_outlier, new_tool and volume_spike. Switching them or changing sensitivity writes a receipt and has no effect; they can never raise a new alert.

It should flag the first fresh receipt whose args_summary vendor, to_domain or to_account was not seen for this agent in the last 90 days: medium when an amount is present, otherwise low. Add `if (on('off_hours'))`. It should flag a fresh receipt whose IST hour-of-week bucket holds 0.5% or less of the 14-day base, scaled by sens(). Alternatively, disable those two switches with a 'Not yet running' note and change '6 detectors' to 4 in AlertsPage.

title: Expired approvals can still be approved; expiry only runs inside the live tick of the open organisation
detail: expireApprovals is called only from startLive's tick. The tick is off when Live updates is switched off, for auditors, and for every organisation that is not open. decideApproval never compares `expiresAt` with now, so a held payment whose expiry passed can be approved and run. Expiry also appends only a receipt (emit 'receipt'), never emits 'approval', so views subscribed to ['approval'] (RulebookPage:144, ApproverGroups:27) stay stale. runEscalations (platform.ts:1278) has the same problem.
repro: Switch Live updates off and wait past a 2-hour deploy approval's expiry (or open an organisation whose approvals expired while another was open). Approve it: it is accepted and the outcome is 'ok'.
fix: In db.ts decideApproval, after the status check, add `if (Date.now() >= new Date(a.expiresAt).getTime()) { expireApprovals(db); throw new Error('This approval expired. Expiry is a refusal.'); }` and add the same check in issueApprovalLink. Call expireApprovals(db) at the start of api.approvals / api.approval for any organisation. At the end of expireApprovals (and runEscalations), call emit(db.org.id, 'approval') when anything changed (export or reuse touch()).
verifyNote: Partly confirmed. expireApprovals (db.ts:891) runs only in the live tick, which is off when Live updates is off or for auditors (AppShell.tsx:65), and only for the open organisation. decideApproval does not compare expiresAt, and neither does work/backend.decide. The UI paths do guard: ApprovalDetail computes expiredNow and hides the decision form, and decideByLink checks link expiry. So the hole is at the api level plus stale state. The second part is confirmed: expiry only calls append (emit 'receipt'), never emit 'approval', so views subscribed to ['approval'] stay stale.

title: Dual control: publish accepts any YAML or rules, not the content that was reviewed
detail: At L2 and above, publishRulebook checks only that an approved review exists for `version`. It then signs whatever `yaml/rules` the caller passes; the review does not store the draft hash and nothing compares against it. Only the PublishTab UI blocks a dirty editor. A direct api.publish call, or any other caller, can publish unreviewed rules under someone else's approved review, with `reviewed_by` set on the receipt.
repro: Get v8 approved by a reviewer, then call api.publish(org, rb.id, differentYaml, differentRules, â€¦): it publishes, and the receipt says dual_control enforced, reviewed_by = the reviewer.
fix: In platform.ts requestReview, store `draftHash: draft.hash` on the ReviewRequest. In db.ts publishRulebook, when `enforced`, require `sha256Hex(yaml) === review.draftHash` (else throw 'Dual control: this content is not the version that was reviewed'), or ignore the caller's yaml and rules and publish draft.yaml and draft.rules.
verifyNote: Confirmed at db.ts:1067-1086. publishRulebook checks only that an approved review exists for `version`, then signs whatever yaml and rules the caller passes. ReviewRequest stores no draft hash. saveDraft does invalidate reviews when the stored draft changes, and PublishTab blocks a dirty editor, so the UI path is safe. A direct api.publish call can still publish unreviewed content under someone else's review, with reviewed_by on the receipt. Downgraded to medium because it is reachable only through the api.

title: Most api mutations enforce no role server-side
detail: These api mutations, and the db/platform functions behind them, check no caller role at all: setAgentStatus, createAgent, revokeKey and issueKey (176-199); saveDraft and publish (no 'rulebooks.publish'); setToolEnabled and addUpstream; rotateKey (303); reviewAssessment (342, only checks author â‰  reviewer, not 'assessments.signoff', and re-approves already decided assessments); setFramework; setAlertStatus; engageStop and liftStop (396-403); revokeDisclosure (598, no role or level check); signCheckpoint; and exportPack. A viewer or approver session can do all of these by calling api directly; only the UI hides the buttons. revokeKey and issueKey also crash with a non-null assertion on an unknown slug or key.
repro: Signed in as u_meera (viewer), run `api.engageStop('org_demo','u_meera','x')` or `api.rotateKey('org_demo','u_meera')` from the console: both succeed and are recorded.
fix: Add `requirePerm(orgId, userId, perm)` in api/index.ts, built on the member-record role (see finding 2) and lib/permissions can(). Call it first in each mutation: stop.engage for engageStop and liftStop, agents.pause, agents.keys, rulebooks.edit for saveDraft, rulebooks.publish, connectors.manage, settings.security for rotateKey, assessments.signoff (also require a.status === 'submitted'), compliance.manage, alerts.manage, and evidence.checkpoint and evidence.export. Replace each `find(...)!` with a lookup that throws a 'Not found' Error.
verifyNote: Confirmed in api/index.ts. setAgentStatus, createAgent, revokeKey and issueKey (176-199), saveDraft and publish (242-249), setToolEnabled and addUpstream (256-278), signCheckpoint, exportPack and rotateKey (289-306), reviewAssessment (342: no assessments.signoff check, and it re-decides assessments that are not 'submitted'), setFramework, setAlertStatus, and engageStop and liftStop (396-403) perform no role check. revokeKey, issueKey, setSuggestion, setToolEnabled, setFramework and setAlertStatus use `!` and crash with a TypeError on an unknown id. The backend is an in-browser mock and the UI hides the controls, so this is medium, not high, but it contradicts platform.ts and orgApi, which do enforce roles.

title: deriveBilling retroactively re-prices every past (paid) invoice on upgrade, pack install or seat change
detail: deriveBilling rebuilds all months from April with the CURRENT plan floor, `MODELLED_SCALE[current plan]` and the CURRENT pack and seat counts. It is called from upgradeLevel, installPack, addCounterparty and setCounterpartySeats, so upgrading Demo Traders to L2 turns Aprilâ€“September's 'paid' invoices into L2 floors (â‚¹6,00,000/yr) with 2.4Ã— volumes. Northbank, L2 only for 45 days, already shows L2 floors and the ledger1 pack for Aprilâ€“August, months it spent on L1.
repro: Open Billing on org_demo and note the April total, then upgrade to L2: the April invoice (status paid) changes amount.
fix: In deriveBilling, price each month with `levelAt(db.org.levelHistory, Date.UTC(y, mo-1, 1), db.org.plan)` (plan and scale per month), and charge packs and seats only from their install or `since` date. When called after the initial build, keep existing invoices whose status is 'paid' or 'due' and regenerate only the draft (current) month.
verifyNote: Confirmed at db.ts:453-482. deriveBilling rebuilds every month from April with the current db.org.plan (PLANS and MODELLED_SCALE) and the current pack and seat counts, and marks the earlier months paid and due. It is called again from upgradeLevel (platform.ts:642), setCounterpartySeats (901), addCounterparty (914) and installPack (1138), so invoices already marked paid change amount after an upgrade or a seat change.

title: Invoices count 6 counterparty seats at build, not the seeded register (Kaveri 7, Deccan 5)
detail: buildOrg calls deriveBilling(db) before `db.platform = seedPlatform(db)` (line 372). Inside deriveBilling, `db.platform?.counterparties?.reduce(...) ?? 6` and `db.platform?.packs?.length ?? â€¦` fall back to the hard-coded 6 seats and the per-level pack counts. The invoices therefore disagree with the counterparty register (Kaveri 2+2+1+1+1 = 7 seats, Deccan 5) until something else calls deriveBilling.
repro: Fresh load as u_lakshmi: Counterparties shows 7 seats, while the October invoice line reads 'Counterparty verification seats (6)'.
fix: In db.ts buildOrg, move `deriveBilling(db)` after `db.platform = seedPlatform(db)`, provided seedPlatform does not read db.invoices; otherwise call deriveBilling again after it. Remove the `?? 6` and per-level pack fallbacks.
verifyNote: Confirmed. buildOrg calls deriveBilling(db) at db.ts:365 while db.platform is still `undefined as unknown as PlatformState`, and only sets it at line 372. Inside deriveBilling, `db.platform?.counterparties?.reduce(...) ?? 6` and `db.platform?.packs?.length ?? ...` therefore use the fallbacks. Kaveri's seeded seats are 2+2+1+1+1 = 7 and Deccan's are 5 (platform.ts:257-271), so the invoices disagree with the register until another call to deriveBilling.

title: syncOrgMeta persists the seeded relative level dates as absolute ones, so the level boundary drifts from the chain
detail: getDB calls syncOrgMeta for every organisation it opens, which writes `levelHistory` to eg:levels:v1. Northbank's and Kaveri's histories are relative (daysAgoIso(45), (120), (30)), but applySavedLevels restores the absolute timestamps from the first visit. After the 12-hour state expiry the chain is regenerated against a new NOW0: the KMS and HSM key epochs move with NOW0 but the L2/L3 boundary does not. A day later, records signed by the env key fall inside the 'L2 Attested, key in AWS KMS' sealed range, and 'L2 since 45 days' becomes 46, 47 and so on.
repro: Open org_northbank, then reload more than 12 hours later (or set the clock forward): levelState's boundary is no longer at the key.rotated (k_northbank_kms_2) receipt.
fix: In db.ts getDB, update only the in-memory ORGS entry (Object.assign), and do not write localStorage. Move the localStorage write into a separate `persistLevels(org)` called only from platform.upgradeLevel. In applySavedLevels, skip seeded organisations unless a saved entry has a history longer than the seed's. Alternatively, drop saved levels for seeded organisations whenever loadState discards expired state.
verifyNote: Confirmed. getDB calls syncOrgMeta (db.ts:666, 677), which writes levelHistory to eg:levels:v1 with the absolute timestamps from users.ts daysAgoIso(...). applySavedLevels (91-99) writes them back into ORGS at module load, and specs() clones ORGS (187-190). After the 12-hour state expiry, buildOrg regenerates the chain against the new NOW0: key epochs (from NOW0 - daysAgo*D) move, but the saved level boundary does not. resetDemo clears LEVELS_KEY; the 12-hour expiry does not.

title: No hourly checkpoints after the seeded chain; 'Hourly checkpoints' stops after page load
detail: Checkpoints are created only by generateChain, by buildFreshOrg's genesis and by the on-demand signCheckpointNow (`onDemand=false` is never used). The live engine appends receipts indefinitely without checkpoints, so the L1 capability 'The chain head is signed every hour it moves' is false after load, and a sign-up organisation has only its genesis checkpoint. The MCA profile rule C04 ('a signed checkpoint exists for every day with activity') fails as soon as live traffic crosses midnight IST.
repro: Leave the console on org_northbank with Live updates on across 00:00 IST, then run the in-mca-audit-trail profile: C04 fails for the new day.
fix: In db.ts startLive tick (after governCall), add: `const lastCp = db.checkpoints[db.checkpoints.length-1]; const head = db.receipts[db.receipts.length-1]; if ((!lastCp || Date.now() - new Date(lastCp.ts).getTime() >= H) && (!lastCp || lastCp.seq !== head.seq)) signCheckpointNow(db, false);`. Do the same catch-up once in getDB after loadState.
verifyNote: Confirmed. signCheckpointNow (db.ts:728) is called only from the api's on-demand path (api/index.ts:291), and the live tick (742-758) never signs a checkpoint. The UI claims hourly checkpoints in lib/levels.ts:34, ReceiptPage.tsx:626, ChainPage.tsx:82 and governance EG-03. After load, the head is not checkpointed hourly.

title: Rule quotas (max_count / max_sum per window) are never evaluated
detail: Rules carry `quota` (for example pay-small max_sum â‚¹3,00,000/day, reminders max_count 120/day, sweep 6/day). The rulebook editor validates them and EG-07 claims 'Count and sum quotas per window turn an allow into an ask'. But evaluate() ignores `rule.quota` entirely, and so do replay, Try an action and the live guard. An allow rule stays an allow past its daily cap.
repro: In Try an action for collections-agent, nothing changes no matter how many reminders were already sent today; the RBI C04 profile can fail while the rulebook still allows.
fix: Add an optional `history?: Receipt[]` parameter to evaluate. When the winning rule is an allow with a quota, sum or count the prior receipts in history with rule_id === rule.id, decision 'allow' and ts inside the window (day = since IST midnight), and add the current call. If that exceeds the limit, return decision 'ask', ruleId `${rule.id}:quota` and a reason naming the limit. Pass the agent's receipts from governCall (see finding 5), testOnPast and tryAction.
verifyNote: Confirmed. evaluate() (lib/evaluate.ts:42-58) ignores rule.quota, and so do replay, api.tryAction (the rulebook Try tab) and governCall. Only developers/TryIt.tsx:172-185 simulates quotas with a session counter. The seeded pay-small, reminders and sweep rules carry quotas, and EG-07 claims that quotas turn an allow into an ask.

title: semanticDiff labels threshold changes tighter or looser backwards for gt/gte conditions
detail: `looser = (r.decide === 'allow') === raised` assumes an lte/lt condition. For `gt`/`gte`, raising the threshold matches FEWER calls. The seeded v8 draft raises pay-large (ask, amount gt 50000) to gt 100000, which means fewer payments are held, which is looser. semanticDiff reports it as 'tighter'. The same inversion applies to allow rules with gt.
repro: Open the invoice-bot rulebook's v8 draft diff or review: 'pay-large: amount gt 50000 â†’ gt 100000' is shown as tighter.
fix: In semanticDiff, compute `const up = ['gt','gte'].includes(nn.op) ? false : ['lt','lte'].includes(nn.op) ? true : undefined; const matchesMore = up === undefined ? undefined : up === raised;`. Then use `looser = matchesMore === undefined ? undefined : r.decide === 'allow' ? matchesMore : !matchesMore` (for ask and refuse, matching more is tighter). When on.op !== nn.op or looser is undefined, push change 'changed'.
verifyNote: Confirmed at lib/evaluate.ts:107-109. `looser = (r.decide === 'allow') === raised` assumes an lt or lte condition. The seeded v8 draft (catalog.ts:209) raises pay-large (ask, amount gt 50000) to gt 100000. That holds fewer payments, which is looser, but it is labelled 'tighter' in the diff and review.

title: markReauth overwrites signedInAt: it extends the session lifetime and breaks the session record id
detail: Re-entering the password (stop dialog, publish) sets `signedInAt = Date.now()`. That timestamp is also (a) the start of the org session-lifetime clock in sessionLifetime.ts, so each re-auth restarts an 8h/12h lifetime and a session can live indefinitely, and (b) the session id `ses_${userId}_${signedInAt}` used by orgApi.registerSession and endExpiredSession. After a re-auth, a new session row is created and the old one stays 'active' for ever. Ending the browser's real session from Sessions no longer matches it, and expiry cannot mark it ended.
repro: Sign in, engage a stop after 10 minutes (password prompt), then open Settings â€º Sessions: there are two active sessions for one browser, and the lifetime countdown has reset.
fix: In session.ts, add `reauthAt?: number` to SessionState and to load() and save(). needsReauth reads `reauthAt ?? signedInAt`; markReauth sets only reauthAt. Leave signedInAt unchanged after sign-in.
verifyNote: Confirmed at store/session.ts:85-90. markReauth sets signedInAt = Date.now(). signedInAt is also the session-lifetime anchor (sessionLifetime.ts:24, 37) and part of the session id `ses_${userId}_${signedInAt}` (orgApi.registerSession 260, registry.ts:319 and 344, YouPage 186, Sessions.tsx 23). Each re-auth restarts the lifetime, registers a second session row (the old one stays active), and makes the remote-end and expiry lookups miss.

title: Approvals of a paused agent can still be approved and run
detail: decisionBlocked only covers emergency stops. setAgentStatus(â€¦, 'paused') does not hold the agent's waiting approvals, and decideApproval does not check `agent.status`. Approving a held payment from an agent its owner just paused runs it on the governed run (outcome ok), which is inconsistent with the stop semantics and with 'Agent paused' on its new calls.
repro: Pause invoice-bot from the console, then approve one of its pending â‚¹2,40,000 payments: the receipt shows outcome ok.
fix: In db.ts decisionBlocked, after the stop check, look up the agent: `const ag = db.agents.find(x=>x.slug===a.agentSlug); if (a.status==='pending' && ag && ag.status !== 'active') return `${ag.slug} is paused. Resume it to decide its waiting approvals; their expiry still runs.`;`. decideApproval and issueApprovalLink already call decisionBlocked.
verifyNote: Confirmed. decisionBlocked (db.ts:922-927) covers only emergency stops, and decideApproval does not check agent.status. setAgentStatus(..., 'paused') and the auto-pause leave pending approvals decidable. Approving a held MCP call from a paused agent (for example the auto-paused treasury-sweeper) runs it with outcome ok, while its new calls are refused as 'Agent paused'.

title: Verifier claims 'Key valid when signed â€¦ not retired before the receipt' but never checks it
detail: The 'Key valid when signed' summary line says every key 'was not retired before the receipt', but verifyChain only checks that `keys[r.kid]` exists. A retired key, for example a leaked env key after the KMS move, can sign new receipts and the check reports pass. The bundle's manifest.keys carries status and could support the check.
repro: Re-sign the last receipt of a Northbank bundle with k_northbank_env_1 (retired 45 days ago) and fix up the links: the summary shows 'Key valid when signed: pass'.
fix: Add an optional `keyWindows?: Record<string, { from?: string; retiredAt?: string }>` to verifyChain's opts and set c.key = 'fail' when r.ts > retiredAt for r.kid. Build the windows in verify6 from the key.rotated receipts in the bundle (old_kid is retired at that receipt's ts) or from manifest key status. Until then, change the detail text to 'Every key id resolves to a key in the bundle.'
verifyNote: Confirmed at lib/crypto.ts:151 and 184. The `key` check only fails when the kid is missing from `keys`, but the summary says the key 'was not retired before the receipt'. No retirement window is passed in or checked.

title: Erasure leaves the identifier in plaintext in receipts and in every export
detail: executeErasureOn only records a frozen F14 in `erased`. The affected receipts still carry the matched identifier in `args_summary` (for example to_domain), exportEvidenceBundle (line 716) and exportAuditorPack copy receipts unchanged, and saltFor() re-derives the 'destroyed' salt deterministically. The console and verifier still say the payload 'can no longer be linked to a person'.
repro: Execute erasure DP-2026-0141 on org_kaveri, export a bundle and search receipts.jsonl for the erased domain: it is still present on the affected seqs.
fix: At minimum, change the claims in verify6.ts:356, SealTab, ErasurePage, ReviewsPage:233 and RecordPage:235 to say what actually happens (the payload hash is frozen; the receipt body is unchanged). Better: in exportEvidenceBundle and exportAuditorPack, replace args_summary on erased seqs with { redacted: true } plus the F14 digest, and teach verifyChain and verify6 to accept a redacted body when the seal's F14 is present. Also generate salts randomly per record, store them, and delete the stored salt on erasure.
verifyNote: Confirmed. executeErasureOn (platform.ts:1220-1225) records only the frozen F14 in st.erased. The receipts keep args_summary, which contains the matched identifier (createErasure matched on it), and the exports copy receipts unchanged. saltFor (seal.ts:72-74) is a deterministic sha256 of orgId and seq, so the 'destroyed' salt can always be re-derived. The UI and verifier still say the payload 'can no longer be linked to a person' (verify6.ts:356, SealTab.tsx:76, ErasurePage.tsx:54 and 232).

title: engageStop while a stop is already active orphans the first incident
detail: engageStop has no guard against `db.stop.active`. A second engage overwrites `db.stop` with a new incidentId. liftStop resolves only that one, so the first emergency_stop incident stays 'active' for ever, and Today and Incidents keep showing an active incident.
repro: Engage a selective stop, then engage a full stop and lift it: the first incident remains Active.
fix: In db.ts engageStop, throw `if (db.stop.active)` ('A stop is already engaged. Lift it, or widen it from its incident.'). In TopBar and CommandPalette, disable the Emergency stop action when the stop is active (read d.stop.active, as IncidentsPage does).
verifyNote: Confirmed. engageStop (db.ts:1012-1036) has no `db.stop.active` guard and overwrites db.stop with a new incidentId, and liftStop resolves only that incident. IncidentsPage disables its button while a stop is on, but the TopBar button (TopBar.tsx:79-83) and the command palette do not. After a selective stop, other agents are still active, so StopDialog's count is above 0 and a second engage is possible. The first incident then stays 'active' indefinitely.

title: Re-authentication rewrites signedInAt, which extends the session lifetime and detaches this browser's session record
detail: markReauth() sets signedInAt to now. signedInAt is also the session's identity (`ses_${userId}_${signedInAt}` in registry.watchSession, YouPage and endExpiredSession) and the start of the organisation's session lifetime (sessionLimit). After any re-auth (stop, approvals, publish, upgrade, autonomy), the 8h/12h/24h lifetime restarts. The orgApi session entry for this browser no longer matches: 'This browser' disappears from You â€º Sessions, and unless YouPage re-registers it, ending the session remotely or resetting the password does not sign this browser out, because watchSession looks up an id that is not in the list.
fix: Same as finding 15: add a reauthAt field in store/session.ts (persisted in save and load); needsReauth uses reauthAt ?? signedInAt, and markReauth writes only reauthAt.
verifyNote: This duplicates finding 15 and is confirmed the same way: markReauth (session.ts:85-90) overwrites signedInAt, which is also the session id key (registry.ts:319 and 344, YouPage:186, Sessions.tsx:23, orgApi.registerSession) and the lifetime anchor (sessionLifetime.ts:24, 37).

title: Agent map node links to /assurance/counterparties?id= and /agents/people?member= use params their targets ignore

title: Agent slug 'suggestions' is not reserved, so that agent's rulebook is unreachable
detail: A rulebook's slug equals its agent's slug (mock/db.ts:1116, catalog.ts:195) and is opened at /rulebooks/:slug. title: Unvalidated ?tab= renders an agent page with no body
detail: `const tab = (params.get('tab') as TabId) || 'overview'` accepts any string. A stale or mistyped link such as ?tab=rules or ?tab=activity selects no tab and renders nothing below the tab strip. Other pages validate against a TABS list.
fix: In AgentDetailPage.tsx:57, use `const TAB_IDS: TabId[] = ['overview','rulebook','keys','autonomy','behaviour','approvals','settings']; const raw = params.get('tab') as TabId; const tab = TAB_IDS.includes(raw) ? raw : 'overview';`.
repro: Open /agents/invoice-bot?tab=rules. The tab strip shows no selection and the body is empty.
verifyNote: Confirmed. AgentDetailPage.tsx:57 casts any string to TabId. The body renders only for the seven known values (lines 209-215), so an unknown ?tab= shows an empty body with no tab selected. No internal link currently uses a bad value, so it is reachable only from stale or hand-typed URLs.

title: An old error stays in the Add endpoint dialog when it is reopened
detail: AddEndpointDialog shows `add.error?.message` from useMutation. useMutation clears the error only when mutate runs again, and the dialog's reset effect clears url, events and tried but not the error. After a failed add (e.g. a duplicate URL), cancelling and reopening shows the old red banner over an empty form.
fix: Add `reset = useCallback(() => setError(undefined), [])` to useMutation's return value, and call add.reset() in the Add endpoint open handler (setAddOpen(true)) or in the dialog's open effect. Or pass `error={addOpen ? localErr : undefined}` with local state that is cleared on open.

title: 'Show the records behind this line' shows the wrong set of receipts
detail: linesHref maps inside and beyond lines to /activity?d=allow and refused lines to d=refuse. title: The disclosure 'Your key' check pins the package's own key, so it always passes
detail: PackageDrawer computes fp from pkg.publicKey and passes it as pinnedFingerprint to verifyDisclosure. A package whose key was swapped would still report the key check as passing, although the panel says the counterparty compares 'with one they obtained from you directly'.

verifyNote: Confirmed. DisclosurePage.tsx:353 computes fp from pkg.publicKey and pins that same value at line 358, so the 'Issuer key' step (lib/disclosure.ts:82) is a tautology and can never fail. A mismatch cannot be produced from the UI, so the impact is a misleading 'pass' rather than an exploitable bypass.

title: Open as draft marks the suggestion drafted before saving the draft, and builds YAML without the org's groups and lists
detail: openAsDraft calls api.setSuggestion(...'drafted') and only then api.saveDraft(); if saveDraft throws (e.g. role or validation), the suggestion is left 'drafted' with no draft and disappears from the Open tab. The parse/build context passed to parseRulebookYaml/buildYaml omits `groups` and `lists`, so approvers are generated from the catalogue APPROVER_GROUPS and the org's custom named lists are dropped unless they differ from defaults â€” the saved draft's YAML differs from what the editor would write.
fix: src/features/rulebooks/SuggestionsPage.tsx openAsDraft: build `const ctxBase = { slug: rb.slug, owner: rb.agent.ownerId, approverIds: rb.approverGroups.map(g => g.id), groups: api.approverGroups(orgId), lists: namedLists(orgId) }`, importing namedLists from '@/features/work/backend'. Use `{...ctxBase, version: base.version}` for the parse and `{...ctxBase, version: N}` for buildYaml. Call api.saveDraft before api.setSuggestion.
repro: Make saveDraft fail (e.g. a viewer forced via devtools) or edit approver group members, then Open as draft: suggestion moves to 'Opened as draft' with no draft / draft YAML lists catalogue approvers.
verifyNote: Partly confirmed. The ordering half is real in code (setSuggestion at :71 runs before saveDraft at :72), but db.saveDraft (db.ts:1091) has no role or validation check and does not throw in practice, so the half-state is effectively unreachable. The ctx half is real: both ctx objects at :64/:69 omit groups and lists, unlike RulebookPage.tsx:80. buildYaml therefore writes catalogue APPROVER_GROUPS members via rulebookYaml and DEFAULT lists, unless the base YAML already carried custom ones as extras. finalYaml then publishes that text unchanged if it is not edited, so the signed YAML can show stale approvers or lists. Impact is mainly on the displayed and signed YAML text, so the severity is lowered.

title: Key-custody detail always says the newest receipt 'verifies', even when the row is an outage
detail: The row status comes from `ok = verifySig(...)`, but the detail text is fixed as 'â€¦is signed by ${c.kid} and verifies.' A failed signature shows Outage next to text saying it verifies. The sentence also names c.kid while the check uses head.kid, and these can differ after a rotation.

verifyNote: Confirmed. In StatusPage.tsx:85-88 the status comes from `ok`, but the detail sentence always says 'verifies' and names c.kid, while the check uses head.kid.

title: 'Show #N in the table' lands on page 1 when a filter or search was active
detail: The focus effect calls setFilter('all'), setQ('') and setPage(target). On the next render, the [filter, q] effect sees the changed filter or q and calls setPage(0), which overrides the target page. The row is then not rendered, so the delayed querySelector finds nothing and nothing scrolls or focuses.
repro: Run the FAIL_INTEGRITY sample, switch the table to 'Failing' or type in the search, then press 'Show #N in the table' for a row beyond the first 50.
fix: Remove the effect at line 53. Reset the page in the handlers instead: `onChange={(v) => { setFilter(v); setPage(0); }}` on the Segmented and `onChange={(e) => { setQ(e.target.value); setPage(0); }}` on the SearchInput.
verifyNote: Confirmed. The focus effect (ReceiptTable.tsx:55-68) sets filter, q and page. On the next render the `[filter, q]` effect at line 53 fires because those values changed and calls setPage(0), overriding the target page. The row is not rendered, so the scroll and focus find nothing.

title: ?input=disclosure only selects the Paste tab on first mount
detail: `tab` is initialised from wantsShared once. The footer link 'Verify a counterparty receipt' (/verify?input=disclosure) clicked while already on /verify shows the shared-record banner but leaves the 'Drop or choose a file' tab selected.
fix: Add `useEffect(() => { if (wantsShared) setTab('paste'); }, [wantsShared]);` in VerifyPage.
verifyNote: Confirmed. In VerifyPage.tsx:31 `tab` is initialised once from wantsShared. The /verify footer link (verify/PublicChrome.tsx:65) to ?input=disclosure does not remount the page, so the Paste tab is not selected.

title: Single-key shortcuts navigate behind open dialogs and ignore role limits
detail: The global keydown handler only skips typing targets. With a Dialog or Drawer open and focus on one of its buttons, 'g' then a key or digit navigates the page underneath while the dialog stays open, and '/' opens the palette on top. G+W goes to /auditor and G+B to /billing for any role (line 91 uses ALL_NAV without the roles filter). ShortcutsDialog also lists 'Go to Auditor workspace' and 'Go to Meter' for every role.
fix: At the top of onKey, after the Ctrl+K check: `if (document.querySelector('[role=dialog][aria-modal=true]')) return;`. Apply the role filter from #5.
verifyNote: Confirmed. The window keydown handler (AppShell.tsx:81-97) skips only typing targets. useFocusTrap intercepts only Escape and Tab, so 'g' plus a key with focus on a dialog button navigates the page underneath while the dialog stays open (stopOpen and shortcutsOpen persist across routes). The role part duplicates #5.

title: Escape in capture phase closes the dialog underneath instead of the menu or palette on top
detail: useFocusTrap listens for keydown on document in the capture phase and calls stopPropagation on Escape. Escape therefore never reaches a Menu open inside the dialog, or the command palette (z-80) opened over a dialog. The dialog closes and the menu or palette stays open.
fix: In useFocusTrap's onKey, handle Escape only when `ref.current?.contains(e.target as Node)` (or `document.activeElement`). Otherwise return and let the event reach the palette or the inner component.
verifyNote: Partly confirmed. A Menu inside a Dialog unmounts with the dialog, so that half of the claim does not hold. The palette case is real: Ctrl+K opens the palette (z-80) over an open dialog because the trap does not block it. Escape then reaches the trap's document capture listener first, which stops propagation and closes the dialog underneath, while the palette's React onKeyDown never runs and the palette stays open.

title: Mobile navigation sheet has no Escape, focus handling or footer links
detail: MobileNavSheet is a plain overlay. It has no role=dialog or aria-modal, Escape does not close it, focus is not moved into it or trapped, and it omits NAV_FOOT, so Developers and 'Verify a receipt' cannot be reached from the mobile menu.
fix: In MobileNavSheet, use useFocusTrap (export it from overlay.tsx) or render through Drawer, adding role='dialog', aria-modal='true' and aria-label='Navigation'. In AppShell, append NAV_FOOT.map(it => <Link â€¦>) after the doors inside the sheet.
verifyNote: Confirmed. MobileNavSheet (TopBar.tsx:109-119) has no role=dialog or aria-modal, no Escape handler and no focus trap. AppShell's sheet content renders only DOORS, not NAV_FOOT, so Developers and 'Verify a receipt' are missing from the mobile menu. They are still reachable through the palette.

title: 'Read the format' goes to the docs overview instead of the Action Receipts page
detail: The Action Receipt format is documented at /developers/cross-org, but the button links to /developers, the 'How a call is governed' overview.

title: 'Invitations sent' outbox on the Done step is not filtered to this organisation
detail: DemoOutbox gets orgId={undefined}, so it shows the newest messages from the whole browser outbox (password resets, WhatsApp codes, other organisations' invitations) up to invites.length + 1, under the heading 'Invitations sent'.
fix: Pass `orgId={orgId}` (thread orgId into DoneStep) and `limit={res.invites.length}`. Ideally filter to the emails in res.invites as well.
verifyNote: Confirmed. OnboardingPage.tsx:790 passes orgId={undefined}, so outbox() returns the newest messages from every organisation in the browser. The +1 in the limit shows at least one unrelated message under 'Invitations sent'.

title: Panel actions are shrink-0, so long action text overflows on receipt pages at L2 and above
detail: Live at 375px on /activity/<seq> for org_northbank and org_kaveri (for example /activity/1568 and /activity/1525): the page is 380px wide against a 365px viewport. The 'All fields' panel actions ('12 of 22 receipt fields present Â· Seal v6: 16 of 16 frozen fields', ReceiptPage.tsx:227-230) sit in `flex items-center gap-2 shrink-0` inside a non-wrapping header, so they push past the edge.
fix: In Panel, change the header to `flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-3 gap-y-1` and the actions wrapper from `shrink-0` to `min-w-0` (keep `ml-auto`).
verifyNote: Plausible and consistent with the code. The Panel header (layout.tsx:47) is non-wrapping flex, and the actions wrapper is `shrink-0`. ReceiptPage's 'All fields' actions span (about 70 characters) cannot shrink or wrap, so it overflows at 375px.

title: Verifier report claims 'checked against the key you supplied' when no key was supplied
detail: Live on /verify with the 'One receipt' sample and no fingerprint pinned: the result is 'PASS_KEY_FROM_BUNDLE, Pass â€” key taken from the bundle', but report section 2 (Claim) says 'One receipt, checked against the key you supplied.' The claim text for kind 'receipt' is hard-coded and does not look at whether a key was pinned. All the other samples returned the expected codes: L1â€“SOV PASS_KEY_FROM_BUNDLE (exit 0), FAIL_INTEGRITY 1, FAIL_PROFILE 2, INCOMPLETE 3, UNSUPPORTED 4, USAGE 5, disclosure and counterparty PASS.
fix: In fromBundleResult, build the receipt claim from the options: `o.fingerprint?.trim() ? 'One receipt, checked against the key you supplied.' : 'One receipt, checked against the key in the file (no key pinned).'` and keep the rest of the sentence.
verifyNote: Confirmed. bundle.ts:391 hard-codes 'checked against the key you supplied' for kind 'receipt', regardless of o.fingerprint or a PASS_KEY_FROM_BUNDLE variant.

title: /work/channels#routing never scrolls to the Routing panel
detail: ChannelsPage renders <Panel id="routing"> (ChannelsPage.tsx:210), but React Router does not scroll to hashes on client navigation. AppShell also calls window.scrollTo(0,0) on every pathname change (AppShell.tsx:70), and ChannelsPage has no hash handler. 'Routing and escalation' lands at the top of Channels.
fix: In ChannelsPage, copy the ErasurePage pattern: `const location = useLocation(); useEffect(() => { if (!data || !location.hash) return; document.getElementById(location.hash.slice(1))?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' }); }, [data, location.hash]);`. Make sure Panel forwards `id` to its root element.
repro: Work â€º Not done â€º an 'Approval expired' cluster â€º 'Routing and escalation'. The page opens at the top.
verifyNote: Confirmed. NotDonePage.tsx:400 links to /work/channels#routing. ChannelsPage.tsx:210 renders Panel id="routing", but nothing scrolls to a hash: AppShell.tsx:70 calls window.scrollTo(0,0) on every pathname change, and ChannelsPage has no hash handling. Only ErasurePage.tsx:37 and DevelopersPage.tsx:42 handle hashes.

title: Behavioural alerts can be acknowledged/resolved without a role check
detail: setAlertStatus() requires owner/admin only for assurance alerts; for family 'behaviour' it calls api.setAlertStatus (api/index.ts 378) which has no permission check (and does not set resolvedBy). Only the UI hides the buttons, so any member (viewer, approver) calling the API changes alert state and writes a signed alert.resolved receipt in their name.
fix: In work/backend.ts setAlertStatus, move `requireRole(orgId, userId, ['owner','admin'], 'Owners and admins acknowledge and resolve alerts.')` above the `if (a.family === 'behaviour')` branch. In api/index.ts setAlertStatus, set `a.resolvedBy = userId` when the status is resolved.
repro: As a viewer, call setAlertStatus(orgId, behaviourAlert, 'resolved', viewerId) from the console: it succeeds.
verifyNote: Confirmed in code. setAlertStatus (backend.ts:891-895) delegates behavioural alerts to api.setAlertStatus (api/index.ts:378-386), which has no role check and never sets resolvedBy. The assurance branch does run requireRole. In the UI, AlertPage disables the buttons through useCan('alerts.manage'), so the gap is reachable only by a direct call. Severity is low, not medium.

title: explainRefusals has no role check and does not enforce the L2+ note requirement
detail: NotDonePage gates 'Mark explained' to approvals.decide/rulebooks.edit and requires an 8-character note at L2 and above (NotDonePage.tsx 91, 498), but explainRefusals() accepts any userId and an empty note, so the auditor-facing 'why each refusal was accepted' rule is UI-only. The Undo toast path (line 84) also withdraws with no note.
fix: In explainRefusals add `requireRole(orgId, userId, ['owner','admin','approver'], 'Your role cannot mark refusals explained.')`. Then add `if (on && atLeast(levelOf(orgId), 'l2') && note.trim().length < 8) throw new Error('Write the operator note â€” required at this level.')`.
repro: At org_northbank (L2) call explainRefusals(orgId, keys, '', viewerId): items are marked explained with no note.
verifyNote: Confirmed in code. explainRefusals (backend.ts:353-365) has no role check and no L2+ note rule. NotDonePage enforces both in the UI only: canExplain at line 41, and an 8-character note at line 498. That makes it a backend-only gap, and the severity is low. Undo withdrawing without a note is acceptable.

title: Work door count double-counts second approvals
detail: FourDoors adds `mine` (every pending approval in the user's groups) and `reviews` = reviewsForMe + secondApprovals.filter(canAct). A pending approval that has a first approval and is in the user's group is counted in both, so 'N waiting on you' is too high.
fix: In TodayPage FourDoors line 291, add only second approvals not already counted: `(queues?.secondApprovals.filter((s) => s.canAct && !(canDecide && isInGroup(orgId, userId, s.approval.approverGroup))).length ?? 0)`.
repro: Give a first approval as user A on a two-person payment; sign in as user B in the same group: the Work door figure counts it twice.
verifyNote: Confirmed. FourDoors (TodayPage.tsx:288) counts every pending approval in the user's group as mine. Line 291 then adds secondApprovals with canAct, which includes pending approvals in the same group that already have a first approval. The same item is counted twice.

title: Today 'Open alerts' KPI excludes assurance-health alerts
detail: KpiRow uses data.openAlerts (api.today â†’ d.alerts, behavioural only) while the Alerts page and the Four Doors figure include assurance alerts at L2+. At L2/L3/Sovereign the KPI disagrees with the Alerts page counts.
fix: Pass queues into KpiRow and define `const all = [...data.openAlerts, ...(queues?.assuranceAlerts ?? [])]`. Use all.length for the value, and all.filter(severity==='high') and all.filter(status==='open') for the sub line.
repro: Sovereign org with a node not ready: Alerts page shows a high open alert, Today 'Open alerts' shows 0.
verifyNote: Confirmed. KpiRow (TodayPage.tsx:172-191) uses data.openAlerts, which api/index.ts:82 builds from d.alerts (behavioural alerts only). FourDoors (line 289) and the Alerts page add assurance alerts from queues.assuranceAlerts (backend.ts:1069,1077). At L2 and above the KPI therefore disagrees with the Alerts page.

title: Incident report names health and stop incidents as started by 'Elan1 Govern (auto-pause)'
detail: incidentReportHtml calls startedByName(i.startedBy) and startedByName(t.actor) without the incident kind, so for system-started health incidents the printed report says 'Elan1 Govern (auto-pause)'.
fix: In incidents/util.tsx incidentReportHtml, use `startedByName(i.startedBy, i.kind)` at line 136 and `startedByName(t.actor, i.kind)` at line 146.
repro: Download the report of a health incident (e.g. timestamp outage): 'Started â€¦ by Elan1 Govern (auto-pause)'.
verifyNote: Confirmed for health incidents. util.tsx:136 and :146 call startedByName without the kind, and startedByName (util.tsx:36) returns 'Elan1 Govern (auto-pause)' when the kind is missing. The on-screen IncidentPage:149 passes inc.kind correctly. Stop incidents are started by a user, so they are not affected.

title: 'Timestamped within 15 minutes' is never checked: GST C05 always passes and the test vector is a constant
detail: in-gst-einvoice C05 returns `res(rule, [], â€¦)`, so it passes unconditionally even though anchorBatches marks the degraded window's batches 'late' with tokens delayed beyond 15 minutes. verify6 section 6 also never inspects `delaySeconds` or genTime against windowEnd. Seal test vector 27 ('Second timestamp more than 15 minutes late') is `rejects(16 * 60 > 15 * 60)`, a constant true. Vectors 17 and 24 are tautologies too. The reported results claim checks that do not run.
repro: Run the GST profile on org_kaveri: C05 passes although Anchors shows yesterday's late batches.
fix: In profiles.ts C05, give ctx the anchor batches and fail the seqs of any batch where no token's genTime is within 15 minutes of the batch windowEnd. In seal.ts vector 27, build a batch whose token genTime is windowEnd + 16 minutes and assert that the check under test rejects it, instead of a constant comparison.
verifyNote: Confirmed that the check is vacuous: profiles.ts:168-172 always returns res(rule, [], ...) once anchoredSeqs exists, and seal.ts:290 `rejects(16 * 60 > 15 * 60)` is a constant. The repro overstates the impact, though: the degraded window's own summary (platform.ts:529) says the second authority stayed within 15 minutes, so C05 would legitimately pass on the seeded data. The defect is that nothing is actually checked, so this is low.

title: Test on past actions reports autonomy and gate-error decisions as rulebook changes
detail: replay skips only `rule_id === 'agent-paused'`. At L3, receipts whose decision was changed by autonomy (autonomy-a0/a1/a2/a4/a5, with details.rulebook_decision) and gate-error refusals are compared against the draft's rulebook decision, so an unchanged rulebook shows spurious 'changed' rows (for example allow â†’ ask for every A4 payment).
repro: On org_kaveri, run Test on past actions for supplier-payments with the published rules unchanged: A4-allowed payments appear as 'ask â†’ allow' changes.
fix: In replay, filter out `r.rule_id === 'gate-error'`, and compare against `const before = (typeof r.details?.rulebook_decision === 'string' ? r.details.rulebook_decision : r.decision) as Decision` (use it for `from` and the counts).
verifyNote: Confirmed at lib/evaluate.ts:70-80. replay excludes only rule_id 'agent-paused' and compares e.decision with r.decision. Receipts whose decision autonomy changed (governCall sets details.rulebook_decision, db.ts:796) and gate-error refusals appear as rulebook changes. These receipts come only from live traffic at L3 and Sovereign (chain.ts does not generate them), so this is low.

ErasurePage scrolls only to `location.hash` (article id = e.id), and AutonomyPage reads 'show' and 'level' but never 'proposal'. 'Open and decide' in Work â€º Reviews lands at the top of the page without the item.

ErasurePage scrolls only to location.hash (ErasurePage.tsx:37-38), and AutonomyPage reads only 'show' and 'level' (AutonomyPage.tsx:219-221). ReviewsPage uses row.route for 'Open' and 'Open and decide' (322, 327).

title: Meter reconciliation is a tautology (always matched, difference 0)
detail: `events` is `decisions.map(...)`, so `matched: events.length === decisions.length` and `difference` can never be anything but true and 0. The 'reconciliation' compares the meter with itself and never detects a missing or extra billed event.
repro: Any organisation: reconciliation always reads matched, difference 0.
fix: In meterView, reconcile against an independent figure, for example the current month's usage built from the chain (allowed + approved + 0.4 Ã— (refused + expired) for receipts in the window) or the draft invoice's line quantity. Report the real difference and set matched from it.
verifyNote: Confirmed at platform.ts:1427 and 1450. events = decisions.map(...), so `matched: events.length === decisions.length` is always true and difference is always 0. The reconciliation compares the meter with itself.

title: Seeded receipts cite a rulebook version signed after them, and agents act before they were created
detail: rulebookAt falls back to the first published version when none was signed before `t`. Traffic also starts at the window start for every agent without `cfg.createdAt` (line 214). For Kaveri (a 125-day window), devops receipts from about 125 days ago cite rb_devops v1, signed 38 days ago, for an agent created 40 days ago, and invoice receipts cite v5 (signed 80 days ago). The records contradict the rulebook history shown beside them.
repro: Open an old devops receipt in org_kaveri: the rulebook v1 is signed weeks after the receipt's ts.
fix: In db.ts buildOrg, set cfg.createdAt from every agent: `Object.fromEntries(agents.map(a => [a.slug, new Date(a.createdAt).getTime()]))`. In chain.ts traffic, start at max(start, born, first published signedAt of the agent's rulebook). Remove the fallback in rulebookAt (return undefined) and have callers refuse with rule 'no-rulebook' when there is none.
verifyNote: Confirmed. rulebookAt (chain.ts:84-88) falls back to the first published version when none was signed before t. Traffic starts at `cfg.createdAt[slug] ?? start` (214), and db.ts:304 sets createdAt only for hr-screening. Agents with catalogue createdAt daysAgo(40) (devops) or daysAgo(21) therefore act from the start of Kaveri's 125-day window, citing rulebook versions signed later.
